chunks: And it was narrated from Dāwūd al-Ṣarmī that he said:
A man asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in khazz that is mixed with rabbit fur, so he wrote: “That is permissible.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer whose validity is being asked about
key_terms.الْأَرَانِبِ: rabbits, the source of the fur mentioned in the question
key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, a type of woven fabric or garment material mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.ذَلِكَ: that; referring to praying in that described garment
key_terms.وَبَرِ: fur or fine hair, here referring to the material mixed into the garment
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: it is permissible; a direct legal ruling of allowance

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in khazz mixed with rabbit fur according to Imam al-Hādī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام concerning salat (prayer) in a garment of khazz mixed with rabbit fur. The Imam عليه السلام replied that praying in such a garment is permissible, making the report relevant to the jurisprudence of clothing worn in prayer.
